elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: “Customer” is defined to include its Affiliates, so the grant to Customer already reaches them; Section 23.4 also expressly names Affiliates, albeit with a written-notice formulation.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant does not extend to contractors. Section 23.5 mentions a “designee,” but prohibits transfer, distribution, assignment, or sublicensing to third parties except as permitted by Section 23.4, which permits only Affiliates and an M&A successor.
The fee-paid licence lasts only “through the end of the Term,” not perpetually.
The rendered language does not state that the fee-paid licence is irrevocable.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly tied to the Term and contains no restriction limiting termination to an uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Transferability is limited to Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition transaction, rather than all successors.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 23.4 expressly grants the licence to Customer and, “upon written notice to M&I,” its Affiliates.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 23.4 expressly makes the licence “transferable to Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition transaction,” and Section 23.5 preserves that permission.
